implemented_requirements.requirement: Board representation with 8x8 grid and initial setup
implemented_requirements.evidence: board.py defines class Board, creates an 8x8 grid, and the setup() method places pieces on the standard squares.

implemented_requirements.requirement: Square attack detection (used for check detection)
implemented_requirements.evidence: board.py implements is_attacked() that checks pawn, knight, king, rook, bishop, and queen attacks.

implemented_requirements.requirement: Move object with flags for castling, en‑passant, promotion, double push
implemented_requirements.evidence: move.py defines class Move with fields is_en_passant, is_castle_king, is_castle_queen, promotion, promotion_needed, is_double_push.

implemented_requirements.requirement: Pawn pseudo‑legal move generation including forward moves, double push, captures, en‑passant, promotion flag
implemented_requirements.evidence: pawn.py and pieces.py both contain a Pawn class with pseudo_legal_moves() that handles these cases.

implemented_requirements.requirement: Utility functions for algebraic notation conversion
Game state tracking (turn, castling rights, en‑passant target, half‑move clock, full‑move number, repetition detection)
implemented_requirements.evidence: game.py __init__ sets these attributes and records positions for repetition.

implemented_requirements.requirement: Full piece set (Knight, Bishop, Rook, Queen, King) with move generation
implemented_requirements.evidence: Only a Pawn class is defined in pieces.py; classes for Knight, Bishop, Rook, Queen, and King are missing, despite being imported in board.py.

implemented_requirements.requirement: Legal move validation (including check, checkmate, stalemate)
implemented_requirements.evidence: No code is present that validates moves against check, determines checkmate or stalemate, or filters pseudo‑legal moves to legal ones.

implemented_requirements.requirement: Application of a move to the board and undo capability
implemented_requirements.evidence: Game class lacks any method that applies a Move to the Board, updates castling rights, en‑passant target, clocks, or move history.

implemented_requirements.requirement: Terminal UI loop that reads SAN input (e.g., "Ke8"), prints board after each move, and announces the winner
implemented_requirements.evidence: No script or function is provided that runs a game loop, parses SAN, or prints the board to the terminal.

implemented_requirements.requirement: Castling implementation (king/queen side) with rights handling
implemented_requirements.evidence: Although Game stores castling_rights and Move has castling flags, there is no logic that generates or executes castling moves.
Move includes a promotion field, but no code selects a promotion piece or replaces the pawn on the board.

critical_issues: Missing definitions for Knight, Bishop, Rook, Queen, and King classes – the game cannot represent a full chess set.
No move‑execution logic: the Game class never updates the board, turn, castling rights, en‑passant square, or clocks.
No check/checkmate detection or enforcement; is_attacked() exists but is never used to validate moves or end the game.
No terminal interface or main entry point to accept user input, display the board, or declare a winner.
Incomplete handling of special moves: castling and pawn promotion are only hinted at in data structures, not implemented.
judge.summary: The submitted files contain a partial foundation (board grid, attack detection, a Move class, pawn move generation, and utility helpers) but lack the majority of required functionality. Critical components such as the full set of piece classes, move execution, legal‑move validation, check/checkmate enforcement, castling, promotion, and a terminal UI are absent. Consequently the program is far from a playable, complete chess game and is unlikely to run successfully.
